verdict.root_cause: At 18:23:13 UTC platform automation updated shippingservice's image reference to a tag whose suffix names a different service, and the pod has been unable to reach a serving state since: from 18:23:34 onward shippingservice logs contain nothing but repeated process-startup banners, at least ten of them, tightening into a ~64s backoff cadence through 18:30:02, with no request handling logged after 18:23:34 (it was answering GetQuote and ShipOrder normally at 18:16). The boot output after the change is JVM/OpenTelemetry-Java-agent banners while the pre-change lines were a Rust-style format — a runtime mismatch consistent with the wrong artifact being pulled. With no serving shipping backend, checkoutservice's ShippingService/GetQuote client span is the innermost ERROR in every failing trace, failing in 0.3–2.5ms with no stall signature, aborting PlaceOrder inside prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart and propagating up to the frontend HTTP POST — which matches checkout's logs going quiet on all post-placement steps (payment, email, message write) from ~18:25:44 while placements keep arriving, and matches shippingservice emitting no calls_total series at all for the window. The running artifact on shippingservice is not the one that should be running; that is the mechanism.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge on shippingservice as the failing component and on the 18:23:13 image update as what made it fail. (1) Traces localize the fault precisely: tr_326965fece2e shows the checkoutservice→ShippingService/GetQuote client span is the only ERROR-bearing leaf in every failing trace, with cart, catalog and currency children all succeeding fast, and frontend/checkout error status only inherited. It also rules out latency as the mechanism — failures return in single-digit milliseconds, the signature of a refused/unavailable backend, not a slow one, which excludes dependency_latency. (2) tr_bf2af5a3921f shows shippingservice in a restart loop with backoff, serving normally at 18:16 and never reaching a serving state after 18:23:34, and tr_0788c8691756 corroborates from a different source: no calls_total series at all for shippingservice, numerator or denominator, consistent with a process that never gets far enough to emit RPC metrics. (3) tr_b63725f95c2b supplies the mechanism-defining detail — the new image tag names a different service, and the pre-change reference is unrecorded. That the post-change boot output is JVM-based where the pre-change request logs were Rust-formatted is independent corroboration that a different artifact is now running. This is bad_deploy rather than bad_config: the failing value is an image reference pointed at the wrong artifact, which the taxonomy assigns to bad_deploy. It is not resource_exhaustion — no memory, CPU, fd or connection saturation data was returned anywhere (tr_0788c8691756, tr_69afa240783f), and the crash-without-stack-trace pattern is equally consistent with an image that simply cannot start. Checkout itself is exonerated as the origin: tr_3cd2eeba1e55 records no change on checkoutservice in the bracketing window, tr_be6701c0ec7a shows the process alive and accepting placements throughout with no error lines of its own, and tr_69afa240783f shows an intermittent, non-total error fraction consistent with an upstream partial failure. The correct fix is to restore the previous image reference; a plain restart would only re-enter the same loop.
open_questions: The restart cause is inferred, not observed: no exit codes, container termination reasons, OOM-kill records, or liveness-probe events were retrieved. An image that cannot start and an image killed for exceeding a limit look identical in these logs.

tr_bf2af5a3921f flags that the pre- and post-18:23 log lines come from apparently different runtimes under one selector, and explicitly warns this could be a label collision or a sidecar sharing the service label. If so, the restart loop may belong to another pod and the wrong-artifact reading weakens considerably. This should be confirmed against the pod/container identity before rollback.
The prior image reference is recorded as absent/unknown (tr_b63725f95c2b), so there is no established good version to roll back to — the rollback target must be recovered from deployment history.

No server-side shippingservice span was captured for any failing GetQuote (tr_326965fece2e), so the exact failure mode on the checkout→shipping edge (connection refused, DNS failure, unhealthy endpoint removal) is unmeasured.

shippingservice metrics returned an empty denominator (tr_0788c8691756); the specialist could not distinguish a service emitting nothing from a wrong metric selector, so the metric evidence corroborates but does not independently confirm the outage.

Coverage gaps remain: checkoutservice changes were queried only over 18:16–18:31, leaving ~17:26–18:16 unexamined, and checkout logs are missing 18:16:13–18:25:44, so the precise onset relative to the 18:23:13 deploy is not directly observed.
Whether the other 9 services in the 12-service blast radius are independently affected or are purely downstream of the checkout failure was not dispatched on.
